answer: Trust must arrive from strangers on separate branches. The atlas charts every identity by funding trail and host into 64 branches. A yarrow, one claimed identity, is seated only when peers from distinct branches each spend a tide, a once-per-epoch signed vouch, on it, and no branch may ever vouch twice for one lineage. The k-th yarrow of a lineage needs k fresh branches, so an honest agent costs one tide, while a cloner's eleventh yarrow finds no branch left. Colluding branches or cheaply disguised lineage defeat it.
